What this method does—and what it deliberately does not do

OKLab uses an exact k-d-tree search. CIEDE2000 converts sRGB into CIELAB (D65 white, 2° observer) and finds the exact minimum ΔE00, with kL = kC = kH = 1. It considers the full palette, skipping only entries ruled out by rigorous distance bounds—not an approximate shortlist. Repeated source colors reuse exact results. CIEDE2000 can be much slower, especially with dithering; processing can be cancelled.

Decoding sRGB into linear light is an intermediate conversion, not the distance metric. Both engines then apply nonlinear perceptual transformations. Output is RGBA PNG, so palettes larger than the 256-entry indexed-PNG limit remain intact.

Floyd–Steinberg mode snakes across alternating rows and diffuses RGB error in linear light. This is more physically sensible than diffusing gamma-encoded sRGB values, although any error diffusion trades local accuracy for a better area-average impression.

Neither engine models pixel arrangement, local contrast, or individual vision. Statistics measure the selected engine's distance against the original, uncorrected pixels (not the dither-adjusted input). ΔEOK and ΔE00 use different scales: compare results within the same metric, not their raw numbers against each other. No dithering preserves clean pixel-art regions.

The distance-first 1,024-color profile is a strict subset of the 4,096-color source union. Farthest-point selection and bottleneck-improving swaps prioritize color separation; black and white are retained. Download TXT, GPL, KPL, JSON and swatches.

Static Bloom uses stepped lightness and hue-shifting material ramps informed by Coonie Critters’ terrain and sprite atlases. Its 4,096-color version contains every color in the 1,024-color version. Both keep all pairs above 2 ΔE00. RGB343 is the complete 8 red × 16 green × 8 blue cube, expanded to full-range sRGB. Explore these palettes and download Krita/GIMP files.
